# Transforming Variables {.unnumbered}

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/AAvol-h38zw >}}

## Key concepts/commands:

1.  `destring`: convert a string variable to a numeric variable

    ```         
    destring iep blackhispanic ell thgrmathela, replace ignore("%" "#VALUE!")
    ```

2.  `rename`: rename a variable

    ```         
    rename thgrmathela combined_score
    ```

3.  `gen`: create a new variable

    ```         
    gen z_ell = (ell - 13.79202) / 12.33479
    ```

4.  `log()`: a function to create a log transformation (based on the natural log)

    ```         
    gen log_ell = log(ell)
    ```

5.  `order`: rearrange the ordering of variables

    ```         
    order log_ell, after(ell)
    ```

6.  `drop`: delete variables (or delete observations, as we will learn about later)

    ```         
    drop z_ell
    ```

7.  `egen`: another way to create a new variable, relying on a specific set of functions for creating new variables

    ```         
    egen z_ell = std(ell)
    ```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="r"}
## Model script

``` r
#install.packages("tidyverse")  # uncomment if tidyverse not installed
#install.packages("rio")  # uncomment if rio not installed
library(tidyverse)
library(rio)

data <- import("https://learndata.net/nycschools.dta")

# convert quantitative variables currently
# stored as characters to numbers
data <- data |> mutate(iep = parse_number(iep))
data <- data |> mutate(blackhispanic = parse_number(blackhispanic))
data <- data |> mutate(ell = parse_number(ell))
data <- data |> mutate(thgrmathela = parse_number(thgrmathela))

# rename thgrmathela to something more descriptive
data <- data |> rename(combined_score = thgrmathela)

# log transform the ell variable
data <- data |> mutate(log_ell = log(ell))

# relocate new variable to be next to the original
data <- data |> relocate(log_ell, .after = ell)

# standard ell manually based on summary statistics
#install.packages("psych")  # uncomment if psych not installed
library(psych)
describe(data$ell)
data <- data |> mutate(z_ell = (ell - 13.79) / 12.33)

# drop the standardized variable and then recreate
# it with simpler automated syntax, using scale()
data <- data |> select(!z_ell)
data <- data |> mutate(z_ell = scale(ell))
data <- data |> relocate(z_ell, .after = ell)
```

## Key concepts/syntax:

1.  `|>`: this is called a "pipe" (sometimes also written as `%>%`), here we use it to connect our dataset (`data`) to a data manipulation function (e.g., `mutate()`, `rename()`)[^03-transformations-1]

    ``` r
    data <- data |> mutate(iep = parse_number(iep))
    ```

2.  `mutate()`: create a new variable (or overwrite an existing one), using the `dplyr` package which can be loaded in with `library(tidyverse)`[^03-transformations-2]

    ``` r
    data <- data |> mutate(z_ell = (ell - 13.79) / 12.33)
    ```

3.  `parse_number()`: convert a character variable to a numeric one by ignoring all non-numeric characters[^03-transformations-3]

    ``` r
    data <- data |> mutate(iep = parse_number(iep))
    ```

4.  `rename()`: rename a variable, using the `dplyr` package

    ``` r
    data <- data |> rename(combined_score = thgrmathela)
    ```

5.  `log()`: a function to create a log transformation (based on the natural log)

    ``` r
    data <- data |> mutate(log_ell = log(ell))
    ```

6.  `relocate()`: rearrange the ordering of variables, using the `dplyr` package

    ``` r
    data <- data |> relocate(log_ell, .after = ell)
    ```

7.  `select()`: select only a subset of variables (e.g., all but `z_ell`), using the `dplyr` package

    ``` r
    data <- data |> select(!z_ell)
    ```

8.  `!`: means "not" (e.g., as is "not this variable")

    ``` r
    data <- data |> select(!z_ell)
    ```

9.  `scale()`: standardize a set of values (e.g., from a variable)

    ``` r
    data <- data |> mutate(z_ell = scale(ell))
    ```
:::

[^03-transformations-1]: For a more complete explanation, see <https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html#sec-the-pipe>

[^03-transformations-2]: For more explanation of this and most other functions used in this section, see <https://r4ds.hadley.nz/data-transform.html#columns>

[^03-transformations-3]: For more explanation, see <https://r4ds.hadley.nz/numbers.html#making-numbers>
